data.title: Ichthyosis — viva
data.summary: Disorders of keratinisation · 29 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Ichthyosis** (Disorders of keratinisation)_

**Q1. Describe the process of keratinisation (PYQ).**
- Basal keratinocytes divide → spinous cells (keratins K1/K10 replace K5/K14, desmosomes) → granular layer (keratohyaline granules with profilaggrin, loricrin; lamellar bodies with lipids and enzymes) → stratum corneum: cornified cell envelope (crosslinked by transglutaminase-1) with lipid envelope, extracellular lipid lamellae (ceramides, cholesterol, free fatty acids — 'bricks and mortar'), desquamation by proteases (kallikreins KLK5/7, inhibited by LEKTI) cleaving corneodesmosomes
- Ichthyoses result from defects at any of these steps — increased production (proliferation hyperkeratosis) or decreased shedding (retention hyperkeratosis)

**Q2. Classify ichthyoses (PYQ).**
- Non-syndromic inherited: common — ichthyosis vulgaris (FLG, AD-semidominant), recessive X-linked ichthyosis (STS); autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI) — harlequin ichthyosis (ABCA12), lamellar ichthyosis (TGM1), congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma (ALOX12B, ALOXE3, NIPAL4); keratinopathic — epidermolytic ichthyosis (K1/K10), superficial epidermolytic ichthyosis (K2), ichthyosis with confetti; others — loricrin keratoderma, erythrokeratodermia variabilis, peeling skin syndrome
- Syndromic: Netherton (SPINK5), Sjögren–Larsson (ALDH3A2 — spasticity, intellectual disability, glistening retinal dots), Refsum (phytanic acid), Conradi–Hünermann–Happle (CDPX2 — Blaschkoid, chondrodysplasia punctata), KID syndrome (keratitis–ichthyosis–deafness, GJB2), CHILD (NSDHL — unilateral), trichothiodystrophy (IBIDS), neutral lipid storage disease (Chanarin–Dorfman — lipid vacuoles in leucocytes), Rud syndrome, multiple sulphatase deficiency, ARC, MEDNIK
- Acquired ichthyosis: lymphoma (Hodgkin's), leprosy (LL), HIV, sarcoidosis, malnutrition, hypothyroidism, CKD, drugs (clofazimine, statins, nicotinic acid, kava)

**Q3. Ichthyosis vulgaris — features.**
- Commonest (1:250); onset after 2–3 months of age; fine white/grey scales on extensors (especially shins), flexures spared; palmar hyperlinearity, keratosis pilaris; strongly associated with atopic dermatitis; improves in summer and with age
- Histology: reduced/absent granular layer, compact orthokeratosis

**Q4. Discuss X-linked ichthyosis (PYQ).**
- Recessive X-linked steroid sulphatase (STS) deficiency (deletion Xp22.3) — males; cholesterol sulphate accumulates and impairs desquamation
- Onset at birth/first weeks; large dark-brown polygonal adherent scales on trunk, extensors and flexures, sides of neck ('dirty neck'); palms, soles and face (central) spared; does not improve much with age
- Associations: comma-shaped corneal opacities (asymptomatic, also in carrier mothers), cryptorchidism (testicular cancer risk), ADHD/autism; contiguous gene deletion — Kallmann syndrome (anosmia), chondrodysplasia punctata
- Obstetric: low maternal oestriol (placental sulphatase deficiency) → failure of labour onset/prolonged labour
- Diagnosis: increased serum cholesterol sulphate, rapid lipoprotein electrophoresis (fast-moving LDL), STS enzyme assay, FISH for deletion

**Q5. Describe lamellar ichthyosis and collodion baby.**
- Collodion baby: newborn encased in a shiny, tight, cellophane-like membrane with ectropion, eclabium, flattened ears; sheds in 2–4 weeks; underlying ARCI (lamellar/CIE) most commonly, or self-healing collodion baby (~10%)
- Risks: hypothermia, dehydration/hypernatraemia, infection, poor feeding — nurse in humidified incubator, emollients (white soft paraffin), avoid keratolytics, monitor electrolytes
- Lamellar ichthyosis (TGM1): large plate-like dark scales over whole body including flexures, ectropion, eclabium, scarring alopecia, palmoplantar keratoderma, heat intolerance (hypohidrosis)

**Q6. What is harlequin ichthyosis?**
- Most severe ARCI (ABCA12 — defective lipid transport into lamellar bodies): thick armour-like plates separated by deep red fissures, severe ectropion, eclabium, rudimentary ears, restricted limb movement; high neonatal mortality — systemic retinoids (acitretin) improve survival

**Q7. Write a short note on Comèl–Netherton syndrome (PYQ).**
- Autosomal recessive SPINK5 mutation (LEKTI deficiency) → uncontrolled kallikrein activity → excess desquamation and Th2 inflammation
- Triad: congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma or ichthyosis linearis circumflexa (migratory polycyclic plaques with double-edged scale), trichorrhexis invaginata ('bamboo hair' — eyebrows best), atopic diathesis (high IgE, food allergy, asthma)
- Complications: hypernatraemic dehydration, failure to thrive, sepsis, high systemic absorption of topical drugs (tacrolimus); treatment — emollients, topical tacrolimus cautiously, IVIG, dupilumab/secukinumab (reports)

**Q8. Write short notes on Refsum's disease (PYQ).**
- Autosomal recessive phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase (PHYH) or PEX7 deficiency → phytanic acid accumulation (dietary — dairy, ruminant fat, fish)
- Ichthyosis-like scaling (adult onset, mild), retinitis pigmentosa (night blindness — earliest), peripheral neuropathy, cerebellar ataxia, deafness, anosmia, cardiac arrhythmias, short metatarsals
- Lipid vacuoles in basal keratinocytes on histology; high plasma phytanic acid; treatment — phytanic-acid restricted diet, plasmapheresis

**Q9. Describe Rud's syndrome (PYQ).**
- Rare: congenital ichthyosis + hypogonadism + short stature + intellectual disability + epilepsy (± retinitis pigmentosa); some cases overlap with contiguous gene deletion of X-linked ichthyosis/Kallmann

**Q10. Describe epidermolytic ichthyosis.**
- Autosomal dominant K1/K10 mutation (bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma): blistering and erythema at birth, later corrugated, ridged, malodorous warty hyperkeratosis especially in flexures; histology — epidermolytic hyperkeratosis (vacuolisation of granular/spinous cells with clumped keratohyaline)
- Mosaic form = epidermolytic epidermal naevus; gonadal mosaicism → offspring with generalised disease (genetic counselling)

**Q11. Management of ichthyoses.**
- Emollients and humectants (petrolatum, glycerol, urea 5–10%), keratolytics (lactic acid, salicylic acid — caution for salicylism in children/ large areas, propylene glycol), bath oils, soaking and gentle scrubbing
- Topical retinoids (tazarotene) for localised thick scale; calcipotriol (limited areas)
- Systemic retinoids: acitretin 0.3–1 mg/kg/day or isotretinoin for severe ARCI, epidermolytic ichthyosis, harlequin (lifelong monitoring — bone, lipids, LFT, teratogenicity)
- Eye care for ectropion, ear cleaning, heat precautions, vitamin D supplementation, nutrition, physiotherapy; genetic counselling and prenatal diagnosis
- Emerging: IL-17/IL-23 biologics and dupilumab in some ichthyoses (Netherton, CIE)

**Q12. Define ichthyosis and the difference between inherited and acquired.**
- Disorders of cornification with generalised scaling (fish-like scale) due to abnormal epidermal differentiation/ barrier function
- Inherited: present at birth or early childhood; acquired: adult onset — associated with lymphoma (Hodgkin), malignancy, HIV, sarcoidosis, leprosy, hypothyroidism, malnutrition, CKD, drugs (nicotinic acid, statins, clofazimine, cimetidine, kava, hydroxyurea)

**Q13. Describe the clinical approach to a child with scaling from birth.**
- Was there a collodion membrane (ARCI)? Blisters at birth (epidermolytic)? Erythroderma? Hair shaft abnormality (Netherton)? Neurological/ eye signs (Sjögren–Larsson, Refsum)? Family history and pattern (X-linked — boys; AR — consanguinity)
- Examine distribution (flexures spared in IV), scale type (fine white vs large dark plate-like), palms/soles (hyperlinearity — IV), ectropion/eclabium, alopecia, nails, sweating

**Q14. Ichthyosis vulgaris — pathogenesis and associations.**
- Semi-dominant FLG loss-of-function mutations → reduced filaggrin → reduced NMF, poor hydration; reduced keratohyaline granules (thin/absent granular layer on histology)
- Associations: atopic dermatitis (up to 50%), keratosis pilaris, palmar hyperlinearity, allergic rhinitis/ asthma

**Q15. X-linked recessive ichthyosis — more details.**
- Steroid sulfatase (STS) deficiency on Xp22.3 (mostly whole-gene deletion) → cholesterol sulfate accumulation in stratum corneum → retention hyperkeratosis
- Boys: large dark-brown 'dirty' adherent scales on neck ('dirty neck'), trunk, extensor limbs, with flexural involvement possible; palms/soles spared; corneal opacities (also in carrier mothers), cryptorchidism, testicular cancer risk, ADHD/ autism; contiguous gene deletion — Kallmann syndrome (anosmia, hypogonadism)
- Mothers: low oestriol in pregnancy, prolonged labour (placental STS deficiency); diagnosis — STS enzyme assay, FISH/ microarray, cholesterol sulfate on lipoprotein electrophoresis (increased β-LDL mobility)

**Q16. Lamellar ichthyosis vs congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.**
- Both autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI) — TGM1 (transglutaminase 1), ALOX12B, ALOXE3, NIPAL4, CYP4F22, ABCA12
- Lamellar: collodion baby, then large, plate-like dark brown scales, minimal erythema, ectropion, eclabium, alopecia, hypohidrosis/ heat intolerance
- CIE: fine white scales with prominent erythroderma; less ectropion
- Self-improving collodion ichthyosis — mild residual phenotype

**Q17. Describe the management of a collodion baby.**
- Neonatal ICU, humidified incubator (high humidity), temperature regulation, fluid and electrolyte monitoring (hypernatraemic dehydration), sepsis watch, bland emollients (white soft paraffin), avoid keratolytics (salicylate toxicity), eye care for ectropion, feeding support; membrane sheds in 2–4 weeks

**Q18. Harlequin ichthyosis — features and management.**
- Most severe ARCI — ABCA12 mutation (lipid transporter in lamellar granules); thick plate-like scales separated by deep red fissures, severe ectropion, eclabium, flattened ears, restricted movement, respiratory/ feeding difficulty, sepsis
- Management: NICU, oral retinoids (acitretin 0.5–1 mg/kg) early improve survival, emollients, ophthalmic care; survival into adulthood now possible with severe erythroderma phenotype

**Q19. Epidermolytic ichthyosis — genetics and features.**
- Autosomal dominant KRT1/KRT10 mutations (keratin 1/10 — suprabasal keratins); at birth erythroderma with blisters and erosions; later corrugated, ridged hyperkeratosis especially flexures (cobblestone), malodour, secondary infection; KRT1 — palmoplantar keratoderma
- Histology: epidermolytic hyperkeratosis (vacuolar degeneration of upper epidermis, coarse keratohyaline granules); mosaic epidermolytic epidermal naevus parent → risk of generalised disease in child

**Q20. Netherton syndrome — features.**
- Autosomal recessive SPINK5 (LEKTI deficiency → unopposed kallikrein activity): ichthyosis linearis circumflexa (migratory polycyclic double-edged scaly plaques) or congenital erythroderma, trichorrhexis invaginata ('bamboo hair' — eyebrows best), atopy (very high IgE, food allergy), failure to thrive, hypernatraemic dehydration, infections
- Caution: high systemic absorption of topical tacrolimus/steroids; IVIG, IL-17/IL-4R biologics (case reports)

**Q21. Sjögren–Larsson syndrome.**
- Autosomal recessive ALDH3A2 (fatty aldehyde dehydrogenase) deficiency: ichthyosis (yellow-brown velvety, flexural), spastic diplegia/ tetraplegia, intellectual disability, glistening white dots in the retina (perifoveal), itching; diagnosis — FALDH assay

**Q22. Refsum disease — features and treatment.**
- Autosomal recessive PHYH (phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase) — phytanic acid accumulation: adult onset ichthyosis (vulgaris-like), retinitis pigmentosa (night blindness), anosmia, peripheral neuropathy, cerebellar ataxia, deafness, cardiac arrhythmia, short 4th metatarsal
- Treatment: phytanic acid-restricted diet (avoid dairy, ruminant fat, fish), plasmapheresis during crisis

**Q23. What is KID syndrome?**
- Keratitis–Ichthyosis–Deafness — GJB2 (connexin 26) dominant mutation: erythrokeratoderma-like plaques, spiny hyperkeratosis, PPK (leather-like), vascularising keratitis (blindness), sensorineural deafness, infections, SCC risk

**Q24. What is Conradi–Hünermann–Happle syndrome?**
- X-linked dominant chondrodysplasia punctata (EBP mutation), girls: ichthyosiform erythroderma at birth along Blaschko's lines → follicular atrophoderma, patchy cicatricial alopecia, cataracts, short limbs, stippled epiphyses on X-ray

**Q25. What is CHILD syndrome?**
- Congenital Hemidysplasia with Ichthyosiform erythroderma and Limb Defects — X-linked dominant NSDHL mutation; unilateral (usually right) inflammatory ichthyosiform naevus with sharp midline demarcation, ipsilateral limb defects; topical statin + cholesterol therapy helps

**Q26. Describe topical therapy in ichthyosis.**
- Emollients and humectants: petrolatum, urea 5–20% (stings in children), lactic acid 5–12%, glycerol, propylene glycol 40–60% under occlusion; keratolytics: salicylic acid (avoid large areas in infants — salicylism), α-hydroxy acids, N-acetylcysteine; topical retinoids (tazarotene) for localised thick scale; bathing with oils/ baking soda, mechanical scale removal (pumice)

**Q27. Systemic retinoids in ichthyosis.**
- Acitretin 0.25–0.5 mg/kg/day for ARCI, epidermolytic (lower doses — may increase fragility), harlequin; isotretinoin alternative; side effects — teratogenicity (contraception 3 years after acitretin), mucocutaneous dryness, hyperlipidaemia, hepatotoxicity, skeletal hyperostosis/ premature epiphyseal closure in children (monitor growth, X-rays)

**Q28. What genetic counselling issues arise?**
- X-linked: carrier mothers have 50% risk of affected sons; AR: 25% recurrence; AD (IV, epidermolytic): 50%; prenatal diagnosis by mutation testing/ fetal skin biopsy (historical); consanguinity counselling

**Q29. Complications of severe ichthyosis.**
- Heat intolerance and hypohidrosis (hyperthermia), ectropion/ exposure keratitis, ear canal blockage, hearing loss, growth failure, vitamin D deficiency/ rickets (reduced UV synthesis), infections, contractures, psychosocial impact

## Quick spotter facts
- Fine shin scales + palmar hyperlinearity + atopy — ichthyosis vulgaris (FLG)
- Dark 'dirty neck' scales in a boy + corneal opacities + cryptorchidism — X-linked ichthyosis (STS)
- Collodion baby — humidified incubator, emollients

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Ichthyoses); 2009 Sorèze consensus classification. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
